prompting.creativeDirectorInstruction: You are the senior creative director and image-prompt writer for Burton-on-Trent Golf Club's Event Playbook. Convert the supplied structured event, organiser description, style, output, exact poster copy and organiser data into one sophisticated prompt for GPT Image 2. The organiser's event description is the PRIMARY source of truth for the visual concept. Read it as a creative brief: extract its concrete people, animals, costumes, activities, entertainment, food, setting, jokes, props and unusual features, then deliberately stage the most distinctive of those elements in the finished poster. A vivid or eccentric description must produce a vivid or eccentric visual concept. Never reduce a richly described event to generic golf imagery simply because it is taking place at a golf club. The image model must create the COMPLETE FINISHED EVENT POSTER, integrating campaign artwork and typography into one coherent design. Make the scene concrete, specific and visually directed rather than merely paraphrasing the input. The event concept drives subject matter; the style preset controls treatment only. Treat style names such as 'Cartoon & Playful', 'Photorealistic' and 'Vintage Golf Poster' as internal metadata that must never appear as words, labels, captions or signs in the poster. The supplied club name, event title, event date and price are authoritative copy: instruct the image model to render them exactly, preserving spelling, punctuation, numbers and currency. You may devise concise supporting campaign copy, a subtitle and a call to action when they materially strengthen the poster, but do not invent event facts. Design typography as part of the visual language of the selected style rather than as a generic software overlay. Typography safety is non-negotiable: every required word, date, price, subtitle and call-to-action must be fully visible with generous breathing room. Never place any letterform, text box, badge containing text or essential copy against an image edge. Treat the outer edge as a no-type zone and keep complete words and their containers well inside the output-specific safe area, accounting for any downstream centre-crop. Use clear hierarchy, large readable display text and purposeful poster furniture only when it strengthens the concept. Prefer one strong focal scene, clear storytelling, deliberate depth, expressive detail and premium composition. Before finalising the prompt, perform a silent visual-coverage check: every highly distinctive element from the organiser description should either be visible in the main scene or intentionally represented as a meaningful supporting detail. When adapting an existing primary poster, preserve campaign identity, exact required copy and recognisable artwork while recomposing intentionally for the new aspect ratio rather than inventing a different campaign. Return only the final image-generation or image-edit prompt as plain text with useful section headings. Do not return analysis, JSON, markdown fences or commentary.
globalImageRules: Create the complete finished event poster, including integrated typography and campaign artwork.

The generated image is the finished artwork and must occupy the entire requested frame edge to edge. Never depict it as an inset page, floating poster, bordered print, framed sheet, presentation mockup, canvas-within-a-canvas or smaller design over a blurred duplicate background.
TEXT SAFETY IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: every required word and every text-bearing shape must be completely inside the safe area with visible breathing room on every side.
Never crop, clip, truncate or run any letterform off an edge. Do not let large headline typography touch the top, left, right or bottom boundary.
When adapting artwork to another aspect ratio, deliberately recompose and reflow it. Never use a centre crop that can remove typography, branding or important subjects.
Treat the organiser-supplied event description as a visual brief, not background metadata.
Explicitly show the most distinctive concrete elements from the event description. Unusual people, animals, costumes, performers, food, props and activities should materially shape the composition.
Do not substitute a generic golf ball, golfer, clubhouse or fairway for a richer event story when the organiser has supplied more distinctive visual material.
For playful, theatrical or eccentric events, allow the scene to be joyful, surprising, busy and characterful while keeping one dominant focal idea and clear poster hierarchy.
Use one clear visual idea that communicates the event within a few seconds.
Design for viewing at distance as well as close inspection; headline, date and other essential information must remain highly legible.

Render the Club name only when club branding is explicitly requested. Always render the supplied event title, date and price exactly as provided and treat requested copy as immutable, not suggestions.
Use typography, banners, plaques, ribbons, badges or signboards only when they belong naturally to the selected visual style and improve the hierarchy.
Keep important subjects and essential text comfortably inside safe edges so the poster can be intentionally recomposed into other formats without clipping or cropping content.
Make the result feel commissioned for a premium golf-club event rather than generic stock imagery, concept art or a templated software graphic.
Use supporting detail to enrich the main story without competing with the title, date or central event concept.
If organiser instructions conflict with the event's defining concept, preserve the defining concept and interpret the organiser instruction in a compatible way.
globalExclusions: Do not render the style preset name or any phrase describing the visual style as poster copy.
Do not invent or alter dates, prices, sponsor names, competition details, website addresses or Club names.
Do not misspell, paraphrase, abbreviate or substitute the supplied required poster copy.
Do not include the Event Playbook label, interface elements, watermarks or fake logos.
Unless club branding is explicitly requested, do not include the Club name, BOTGC initials, a crest, shield, monogram, wordmark or any other Club branding.
Do not invent dense blocks of small text simply to make the result look like a poster.
Do not literalise prompt-writing terminology, metadata labels or generation instructions as visual content.
Do not allow decorative poster furniture to overwhelm the central event story or essential information.
Do not ignore, minimise or omit the event's most unusual organiser-supplied details in favour of safer generic golf imagery.

events.name: Steeple Chase
events.description: The Steeple Chase transforms the familiar golf course into a completely different challenge. Players tee off from one hole towards a different green, creating unusual routes across the course and forcing them to negotiate trees, slopes and other features from directions they would never normally encounter. It is deliberately unconventional, fun and unpredictable, rewarding imagination and course management as much as normal golfing ability.

sceneRecipe.centralIdea: Make the absurdity instantly understandable: a golfer is standing on the tee of one hole and deliberately attempting an enormous shot over a ridiculous barrier of mature trees towards the clearly visible green of a completely different hole.
sceneRecipe.primaryScene: Show a comical golfer on a tee box immediately after an ambitious heroic drive, frozen in an exaggerated follow-through and looking slightly alarmed by the decision. Establish a dense wall of tall mature trees as a major obstacle between the golfer and a distant, unmistakably separate green. Show the golf ball on a dramatic high arc over the trees so the route can be understood at a glance.
mustShow: The teeing golfer must be a strong foreground focal point with expressive body language.
A dense and visually substantial wall of trees must clearly obstruct the normal route.
The wrong destination green must be visible beyond the trees and spatially readable as belonging to another part of the course.
The golf-ball trajectory must connect the golfer, tree barrier and distant green into one immediately understandable visual story.
Include a second golfer, caddie or onlooker reacting with disbelief, concern or baffled admiration.
supportingDetails: Include a few woodland animals such as an owl, squirrel, rabbit, fox or deer watching the shot with amused concern.
Use rich foliage, leaves, branches and course contours to make the scene feel specific and storybook-rich.
Small visual jokes are welcome when they remain subordinate to the central golf shot.
If a rustic direction-sign shape is useful compositionally it may appear only as an unreadable decorative object with no legible wording.
moodAndHumour: The humour should come from the ridiculous sporting situation and character reactions rather than from text in the scene.
Make the golfer's confidence and the absurd route feel charmingly at odds with one another.
The overall feeling should be warm, funny, eccentric and inviting rather than slapstick or chaotic.
avoid: Do not show the golfer simply playing a normal straight golf hole.
Do not hide the distant target green behind the trees or make the intended route ambiguous.
Do not make the tree obstacle a minor background feature.
Do not turn the woodland animals into the main subject.
Do not use embedded slogans, hand-lettered event copy or readable direction signs to explain the joke.

events.name: Junior Open
events.description: A welcoming but competitive junior golf event bringing together young golfers for a day of enjoyable competition, achievement and club atmosphere. It should feel energetic, ambitious and friendly, celebrating young people playing golf at Burton-on-Trent Golf Club.

sceneRecipe.centralIdea: Celebrate young golfers taking part in a genuine competitive event while keeping the atmosphere welcoming, positive and full of possibility.
sceneRecipe.primaryScene: Build the image around one or more junior golfers engaged in a meaningful competitive golf moment on a beautiful course, with confident movement, concentration and a visible sense of achievement.
mustShow: Junior golfers should feel capable, engaged and age-appropriate rather than posed like adult professionals.
Golf must be immediately recognisable through authentic course context and action.
The image should balance competition with warmth and inclusion.
supportingDetails: Use course landscape, flags, clubs and subtle spectator or teammate context to create event atmosphere.
Show natural interaction and energy rather than static line-ups.
moodAndHumour: Allow small moments of personality without making the event feel childish.
avoid: Do not portray children as miniature adult professionals in overly formal poses.
Do not make the scene look like generic golf stock photography or a coaching lesson.

events.name: Captain's Dinner
events.description: A formal evening social event with dining, speeches and a traditional golf-club atmosphere. The event should feel polished, warm and prestigious, with a sense of occasion and understated elegance.

sceneRecipe.centralIdea: Create a sense of an important but welcoming Club occasion: beautifully prepared dining, warm hospitality and understated golf-club tradition.
sceneRecipe.primaryScene: Show an elegant clubhouse evening with carefully dressed tables, warm low lighting, polished glassware and guests arriving or enjoying the occasion, with subtle visual cues to golf-club heritage.
mustShow: The dining environment must feel premium, warm and real.
Include enough human presence to communicate a social occasion without making the image crowded.
Use lighting and composition to create a clear focal area suitable for a formal event campaign.
supportingDetails: Tasteful table settings, glassware, subtle floral or traditional decoration and restrained golf-club details.
Warm pools of light and rich material textures.
moodAndHumour: No overt comedy; personality should come through natural human warmth.
avoid: Do not make the scene look like a generic wedding reception or corporate conference.
Do not overdecorate or make the image ostentatious.

events.name: Christmas Party
events.description: A festive clubhouse celebration with dining, music and a lively social atmosphere. The feeling should be warm, seasonal and inviting, with festive colour, clubhouse comfort and a clear sense of fun.

sceneRecipe.centralIdea: Show the clubhouse transformed into a warm festive social occasion that members would immediately want to join.
sceneRecipe.primaryScene: Create an inviting clubhouse Christmas scene with groups of members enjoying a lively evening, warm lighting, tasteful festive decoration and a clear sense of celebration.
mustShow: The clubhouse social atmosphere must be the main subject.
Festive decoration should be obvious but tasteful.
People should look naturally engaged with one another rather than posed.
supportingDetails: Warm fairy lights, greenery, seasonal table details and subtle golf-club context.
Use depth and layered groups to suggest a lively evening without visual clutter.
moodAndHumour: Warm, convivial, celebratory and slightly playful.
The image should feel welcoming to members rather than exclusive or formal.
avoid: Do not make it look like a generic commercial Christmas advert.
Do not overwhelm the scene with novelty Christmas props.

events.name: Custom event
events.description: A Burton-on-Trent Golf Club event. Use the organiser-supplied description as the source of truth for the activity, atmosphere and central visual idea.

sceneRecipe.centralIdea: Translate the organiser-supplied event description into one immediately understandable, event-specific visual idea.
sceneRecipe.primaryScene: Create a strong central scene that shows what makes this event distinctive rather than relying on generic golf imagery.
mustShow: The event activity described by the organiser
A clear golf-club context where relevant
supportingDetails: Use supporting details only when they strengthen the event story
moodAndHumour: Match the selected style and the character of the event
avoid: Generic stock-poster composition
Inventing event facts that were not supplied

styles.name: Cartoon & Playful
styles.summary: Whimsical hand-drawn storybook artwork with warmth, character and humour.
styles.styleDirection: Create a richly observed whimsical British storybook illustration: hand-drawn and characterful, with the warmth and craft of traditional children's picture-book art adapted into a premium golf-club campaign. The treatment should feel genuinely illustrated rather than like a generic cartoon filter.
visualLanguage: Loose but confident hand-drawn ink outlines with natural variation rather than mechanically perfect vector edges.
Textured watercolour and gouache-like washes with visible paper-like warmth and subtle pigment variation.
Warm slightly muted natural colours led by rich greens, earthy browns, creams, mosses and restrained golden yellows.
Expressive faces, hands and body language with gently exaggerated proportions and perspective.
Detailed trees, leaves, branches, grass and environmental storytelling that rewards closer viewing.
Strong silhouette and readable staging so the central joke remains clear from across a room.
Use decorative natural framing only where it supports the composition; never let decorative foliage become typographic poster furniture.
mood: Humorous without becoming childish or visually cheap.
Premium enough to feel commissioned for a real Club event.
avoid: Avoid photorealism, glossy 3D rendering, flat clip-art, generic comic-book styling and slick corporate vector art.
Avoid automatically creating vintage headline lettering, ribbons, badges or printed-poster text merely because the style is illustrative.
Avoid imitating a named living artist; describe the visual characteristics directly.

variations.name: Loose ink-and-watercolour comedy
variations.styleDirection: Stage the event as a lively observational cartoon drawn with fast, broken ink lines and translucent watercolour washes. Use off-kilter perspective, expressive physical comedy and many small background reactions, while keeping the main action and poster hierarchy immediately readable.

variations.name: Cut-paper character collage
variations.styleDirection: Build the scene from irregular hand-cut paper shapes, painted tissue textures, torn edges and layered shadows. Give the characters simple but highly expressive silhouettes and use overlapping collage planes to create depth without becoming slick vector art.

variations.name: Bold screen-print cartoon
variations.styleDirection: Use chunky hand-drawn contours, a restricted four-colour screen-print palette, visible ink overlap and bold comic staging. Favour one exaggerated action, graphic shadows and strong negative space rather than a densely painted storybook scene.

variations.name: Soft chalk-and-pastel story
variations.styleDirection: Render the event in soft chalk, wax crayon and pastel with grainy paper texture, rounded forms and warm diffuse light. Make the humour gentle and character-led, using colour blocking and expressive poses rather than hard outlines.

variations.name: Newspaper ink caricature
variations.styleDirection: Use witty editorial-cartoon drawing with energetic brush-and-pen marks, selective flat colour, purposeful white space and sharply observed gestures. Exaggerate props and poses for humour while keeping people affectionate rather than grotesque.

variations.name: Folk-art gouache tableau
variations.styleDirection: Create a decorative hand-painted folk tableau using opaque gouache, flattened perspective, patterned foliage and rhythmic groups of figures. Let repeated shapes and border-like natural details build charm, but keep all typography separate, spacious and completely legible.

styles.name: Serious & Formal
styles.summary: Elegant, restrained and suitable for premium dinners, presentations and formal occasions.
styles.styleDirection: Create a refined premium editorial campaign image with understated traditional golf-club character, balanced composition and sophisticated visual restraint.
visualLanguage: Controlled, elegant composition with clear hierarchy and purposeful negative space.
Rich but restrained colour, natural materials and subtle atmospheric lighting.
Premium editorial finish rather than corporate brochure imagery.
mood: Formal without feeling cold or inaccessible.
avoid: Avoid corporate conference imagery, excessive luxury clichés and generic black-tie stock scenes.
Avoid embedded typography or ornamental headline devices.

variations.name: Candlelit editorial
variations.styleDirection: Use low-key candlelit or lamplit atmosphere, deep natural shadows, restrained warm highlights and an editorial composition inspired by premium hospitality photography. Keep faces and materials believable and the mood intimate rather than theatrical.

variations.name: Architectural minimalism
variations.styleDirection: Build a calm, symmetrical composition around the clubhouse architecture or course landscape, using precise lines, generous negative space and a limited stone, cream, navy and green palette. Human figures should be small, purposeful accents rather than the dominant subject.

variations.name: Heritage still life
variations.styleDirection: Express the event through an art-directed still life of authentic objects, materials and setting details: polished wood, scorecards, glassware, trophies, flowers or golf equipment as appropriate. Use museum-like light and immaculate spacing without luxury-brand clichés.

variations.name: Monochrome documentary
variations.styleDirection: Use refined black-and-white documentary photography with subtle film grain, controlled contrast and one restrained brand-colour accent. Capture a candid, emotionally credible moment rather than a posed group portrait.

variations.name: Painterly evening
variations.styleDirection: Create a sophisticated painterly scene at dusk with broad controlled brushwork, atmospheric depth and a restrained heritage palette. Let pools of warm interior light contrast with cool landscape tones and preserve generous space for the event hierarchy.

variations.name: Ceremonial portrait
variations.styleDirection: Compose a dignified environmental group portrait with formal but natural posture, carefully balanced spacing and subtle references to the event. Use soft directional light and rich, quiet colour; avoid rows of people staring like a corporate team photograph.

styles.name: Photorealistic
styles.summary: Authentic people, clubhouse and course detail with cinematic photography-style lighting.
styles.styleDirection: Create premium photorealistic campaign photography with believable people, authentic golf-course or clubhouse detail, natural materials and cinematic but credible light. The image should look deliberately art-directed rather than like generic stock photography.
visualLanguage: Naturalistic anatomy, clothing, equipment and course detail.
Cinematic depth, controlled highlights and realistic atmospheric perspective.
Strong photographic composition with clear subject separation and intentional negative space.
avoid: Avoid artificial HDR, overprocessed skin, impossible golf technique and generic stock-photo smiles.
Avoid embedding style labels, poster text or graphic design elements into the photograph.

variations.name: Golden-hour reportage
variations.styleDirection: Photograph the event as candid golden-hour reportage with long natural shadows, backlit atmosphere and unforced human interaction. Use a slightly wider environmental frame so the Club setting contributes strongly to the story.

variations.name: Crisp sports action
variations.styleDirection: Use high-end sports photography with a decisive action moment, fast shutter clarity, compressed telephoto depth and authentic technique. Keep the energy physical and immediate, with spectators or surroundings providing believable context.

variations.name: Cinematic night event
variations.styleDirection: Create a credible night-time or blue-hour photograph with practical lights, controlled colour contrast, atmospheric haze and cinematic depth. Protect skin tones and real detail; do not turn the scene into fantasy CGI.

variations.name: Intimate environmental portrait
variations.styleDirection: Focus on one or two believable people in an environmental portrait, using shallow depth of field, subtle window or open-shade light and meaningful event details around them. Prioritise expression and quiet narrative over spectacle.

variations.name: Elevated course spectacle
variations.styleDirection: Use an elevated wide-angle viewpoint that reveals the shape of the course, movement of participants and scale of the occasion. Keep geometry and people realistic, with crisp layered depth and a strong graphic pattern in the landscape.

variations.name: Clubhouse lifestyle documentary
variations.styleDirection: Create warm interior lifestyle reportage with authentic candid groups, natural mixed light, tactile clubhouse materials and small event-specific details. The scene should feel observed during a real occasion, never staged as generic hospitality stock photography.

styles.name: Modern Graphic
styles.summary: Bold contemporary campaign artwork with clean shapes and strong visual hierarchy.
styles.styleDirection: Create a bold contemporary editorial illustration with simplified graphic forms, strong silhouette, confident negative space and a distinctive modern campaign identity.
visualLanguage: Clean simplified geometry combined with enough texture to prevent a sterile corporate appearance.
Controlled contemporary colour palette with one or two strong visual accents.
Dynamic cropping and strong directional movement where appropriate.
mood: Distinctive on a large digital screen while still readable at small sizes.
avoid: Avoid generic infographic styling, app-illustration clichés and flat stock vectors.
Avoid rendered typography or fake poster copy.

variations.name: Geometric paper cut
variations.styleDirection: Construct the event from bold geometric paper-cut layers with tactile fibres, crisp shadows and a focused palette. Use large intersecting shapes to frame the subject and make the composition feel physical rather than like flat software icons.

variations.name: Swiss editorial grid
variations.styleDirection: Use an asymmetric editorial grid, disciplined negative space, cropped photographic or illustrated fragments and a restrained palette with one vivid accent. Keep the image confident and poster-like without rendering placeholder typography.

variations.name: Bold linocut
variations.styleDirection: Render the scene as a contemporary linocut with carved black marks, rough ink texture, muscular silhouettes and two or three strong spot colours. Use directional cuts to create movement and landscape depth.

variations.name: Duotone screen print
variations.styleDirection: Use a high-contrast duotone screen-print treatment with halftone texture, purposeful misregistration and oversized simplified forms. Let one strong subject dominate while secondary detail appears through pattern and tone.

variations.name: Abstract editorial collage
variations.styleDirection: Combine torn photographic fragments, painted marks, textured colour fields and simple drawn symbols into a sophisticated editorial collage. Make the event subject unmistakable despite the abstraction and preserve a clean text-safe structure.

variations.name: Dynamic isometric scene
variations.styleDirection: Build a stylised isometric scene with simplified architecture, course features and tiny active figures arranged as one lively system. Use dimensional shading and unusual spatial storytelling while avoiding generic tech-diagram aesthetics.

styles.name: Vintage Golf Poster
styles.summary: Classic tournament-poster character with a tasteful nostalgic feel.
styles.styleDirection: Create a painterly illustration with the visual character of classic mid-century sporting travel and tournament art: restrained print texture, confident shapes, natural period-inspired colour and timeless golf atmosphere. Keep it sophisticated rather than kitsch.
visualLanguage: Painterly shapes and subtle print-like texture without fake damage or excessive ageing.
Traditional sporting composition with strong landscape depth and confident human figures.
Muted heritage palette balanced by clear focal contrast.
mood: Premium and evocative rather than novelty-retro.
avoid: Do not render the words 'Vintage Golf Poster' or any other style description into the artwork.
Avoid fake poster headlines, fake dates, invented sponsor copy and decorative typography.
Avoid distressed-paper gimmicks that overpower the scene.

variations.name: 1930s railway travel lithograph
variations.styleDirection: Use monumental landscape shapes, airbrushed gradients, simplified heroic figures and the refined colour economy of a 1930s British railway travel lithograph. Keep surfaces clean and restored rather than artificially damaged.

variations.name: 1950s tournament painting
variations.styleDirection: Create a mid-century tournament illustration with confident painted figures, sunlit course depth, broad brush shapes and restrained period colour. Stage the moment like a classic sporting programme cover, without copying any existing poster.

variations.name: Public-information illustration
variations.styleDirection: Use the direct visual clarity of a 1940s public-information illustration: strong diagonal staging, economical painted realism, purposeful gestures and a limited utilitarian palette. Keep the tone welcoming rather than propagandistic.

variations.name: Art Deco sporting
variations.styleDirection: Use elegant Art Deco geometry, streamlined athletic silhouettes, stepped framing and a luxurious but limited palette of cream, deep green, navy and gold. Let repeated angles and arcs create movement without relying on ornamental text.

variations.name: 1960s offset colour
variations.styleDirection: Use flat offset-printed colour, simplified angular figures, bold negative space and playful mid-century cropping. Add subtle ink texture and registration character while keeping the overall composition bright, clean and graphic.

variations.name: Heritage woodcut
variations.styleDirection: Render the event as a sophisticated colour woodcut with visible carved grain, layered ink blocks, strong landscape rhythm and sturdy human silhouettes. Use a natural heritage palette and crisp visual hierarchy rather than fake antique distress.

styles.name: Children's Book
styles.summary: A well-known historical children's illustrator is selected by name for each new campaign.
styles.styleDirection: Create an original premium children's picture-book illustration with strong visual storytelling, expressive characters and handcrafted warmth. For each campaign, use the separately supplied named historical illustrator as the explicit style reference and follow that selection consistently across every output.
visualLanguage: Make the event readable as one clear narrative moment with expressive gesture, environmental detail and a strong focal silhouette.
Use convincingly handmade marks, materials and surface texture rather than a generic digital cartoon filter.
Keep the composition sophisticated enough for a real Club campaign while retaining the warmth, surprise and visual wit of a memorable picture book.
Integrate required poster text carefully without letting decorative illustration compromise legibility or safe margins.
mood: Playful where appropriate to the event, but never visually cheap or infantile.
avoid: Do not reproduce recognisable copyrighted characters, scenes, costumes, compositions or book-cover layouts.
Do not reproduce or trace a specific existing illustration; create a new event-specific scene.
Avoid generic animation-studio rendering, glossy 3D characters, clip-art and synthetic vector smoothness.
Do not render the illustrator's name, style name or random direction identifier as poster copy.

variations.name: Delicate countryside watercolour
variations.styleDirection: Use delicate natural-history watercolour, fine restrained outlines, accurately observed animals and plants, pale paper, muted botanical colour and a classic English countryside atmosphere. Keep the scale intimate, elegant and gently humorous.

variations.name: Classic pen and ink
variations.styleDirection: Use traditional expressive pen-and-ink drawing with economical hatching, lyrical countryside observation and selective soft colour washes. Favour believable gesture, quiet humour and spacious page-like composition.

variations.name: Ornate fairytale
variations.styleDirection: Use intricately drawn trees, roots, foliage and fantastical environmental detail with sinuous ink contours, subdued watercolour and a slightly mysterious fairytale atmosphere. Make the magic richly crafted and atmospheric rather than frightening.

variations.name: Victorian engraving
variations.styleDirection: Use crisp black-and-white Victorian engraving language: meticulous cross-hatching, formal line work, eccentric proportions and theatrical staging. Keep the result highly legible and allow optional restrained spot colour only when it strengthens the hierarchy.

variations.name: Warm simple line
variations.referenceWork: The Tiger Who Came to Tea
variations.styleDirection: Use deceptively simple expressive line drawing, flat but softly textured colour and warm domestic observation. Give every face and pose emotional clarity while keeping the scene uncluttered, friendly and gently funny.

variations.name: Observational everyday life
variations.styleDirection: Use richly observed everyday characters, natural body language, layered group activity and warm painted colour. Capture convincing small human moments and environmental details with a welcoming, lived-in sense of place.

variations.name: Soft pencil nostalgia
variations.styleDirection: Use soft coloured pencil, crayon and pastel texture with visible grain, glowing seasonal light and tender visual storytelling. Build a warm nostalgic atmosphere through gentle edges, quiet expressions and hand-worked tonal layers.

variations.name: Painted-paper collage
variations.styleDirection: Construct the scene from bold hand-painted paper shapes with torn and cut edges, visible layered fibres, simplified forms and saturated colour. Use rhythmic repetition and tactile collage depth while retaining a clear event narrative.

variations.name: Intricate fantastical
variations.styleDirection: Use carefully rendered pen-and-watercolour fantasy illustration with dense patterned texture, unusual but appealing creatures, cross-hatched shadows and a dreamlike sense of scale. Balance strangeness with warmth and emotional clarity.

variations.name: Bright geometric patchwork
variations.styleDirection: Use simple rounded shapes, vivid geometric colour, patchwork pattern and strong clean design. Build characters and scenery from cheerful blocks of colour while maintaining visual rhythm and an unmistakable central story.

variations.name: Graphic silhouette
variations.styleDirection: Use bold black silhouettes, sharp profile shapes and a very limited palette of striking flat colours. Create theatrical visual clarity through contrast, cut-paper edges and carefully staged negative space.

variations.name: Jewel-toned painterly
variations.styleDirection: Use richly layered painterly colour, luminous jewel-like hues, expressive brush texture and lavishly observed birds, animals or landscape details. Keep the palette vibrant and celebratory without losing subject clarity.

variations.name: Mid-century travel story
variations.styleDirection: Use a charming mid-century illustrated travel-book aesthetic with simplified architecture, elongated figures, hand-painted gouache texture, playful perspective and a restrained period palette. Make the venue feel distinctive, stylish and full of local character.

outputs.name: Clubhouse Digital Display
outputs.purpose: Primary portrait artwork for the Club's 43-inch 4K portrait displays.
outputs.compositionGuidance: Build the complete artwork natively as a tall, full-bleed 9:16 hero poster with a clear visual story readable across a clubhouse room. The artwork itself is the entire 9:16 frame: extend the environment and visual treatment naturally to all four edges. Never create an inset A-series page, floating poster, bordered sheet, framed print, presentation mockup, mat, canvas-within-a-canvas or blurred duplicate background. All required text must sit comfortably inside a generous inner safe rectangle at least 16% in from the left and right edges and at least 10% in from the top and bottom. No title, club name, date, price, badge, subtitle, call to action or supporting text may clip, kiss the edge or be partially obscured. If space is tight, reduce the text size, add line breaks or simplify the layout rather than risking cropped typography.
reservedOverlayZones: Keep the event title completely visible with generous breathing room. When club branding is requested, keep the upper-right safe area visually quiet for the real Club mark that will be applied after generation.
If the event title is long, reflow it over multiple lines or reduce its size. Never allow the first or last characters to touch the image edge.
Keep the event date fully visible beneath the title in a clearly separated line or plaque.
Keep optional price and supporting copy in a secondary zone that remains fully inside the safe area.
Treat the outer 16% on each side and outer 10% at the top and bottom as a strict protection margin for typography.

outputs.name: Email & Social
outputs.purpose: Square campaign artwork for email and social media.
outputs.compositionGuidance: Recompose the approved campaign into a square finished poster. Preserve the defining action, characters, palette, typography character and exact required copy. Keep all typography within an inner safe rectangle at least 10% from every edge. No text or text-bearing badge may touch, clip against or cross the image boundary. If the wording is long, reflow the layout or reduce type size before allowing any clipping. The result must feel intentionally designed for a square social/email asset rather than a crop.
reservedOverlayZones: Reflow the title and date into a compact but prominent hierarchy suitable for a square image viewed on a phone.
Keep the entire title, date, price and any supporting copy at least 8% inside every edge; reduce type size or reflow before violating the safe margin.
Preserve enough of the central scene that the campaign remains recognisably the same event.

outputs.name: A4 Print
outputs.purpose: Portrait poster suitable for A4 printing at 300 DPI.
outputs.compositionGuidance: Recompose the campaign as a complete A-series portrait print poster. Preserve the approved concept, illustration style, typography character and exact required copy. All typography must remain completely inside an inner print-safe rectangle at least 10% from every edge. No letterform, number, word or text container may be clipped or bleed off the page. If needed, reduce type size or reflow the composition to protect legibility.
reservedOverlayZones: Use a strong upper title and date hierarchy appropriate for an A4 poster.
Integrate optional price, supporting copy and call to action into the artwork without weakening the main scene.
Keep the complete title, date, price and all other essential text fully visible and at least 10% inside every page edge.
